source_caption:
🎬 Twelve (2010)

Twelve follows White Mike, a privileged teenager living in New York City who abandons his comfortable lifestyle and becomes a drug dealer after experiencing a devastating family tragedy. Despite growing up surrounded by wealth and opportunity, Mike finds himself increasingly disconnected from the people around him, spending his days supplying drugs to wealthy teenagers who live for expensive parties, reckless behavior, and temporary escapes from reality. As he navigates Manhattan’s exclusive social circles, Mike encounters a complicated world of friendship, addiction, jealousy, and dangerous personal ambitions. Meanwhile, his former classmates and acquaintances become caught in their own struggles involving relationships, family expectations, and the pressure to maintain their social status. When a powerful new drug known as Twelve begins circulating among the city’s privileged youth, the consequences of their reckless decisions become increasingly serious. As tensions rise and relationships deteriorate, a lavish birthday party brings several characters together, setting the stage for a series of shocking events that threaten to destroy their carefully constructed lives. Through its dark atmosphere, emotional conflicts, and intense storytelling, the film reveals the emptiness that can exist beneath wealth, popularity, and privilege. Combining crime, drama, suspense, and a gritty portrayal of teenage excess, Twelve explores addiction, loneliness, grief, betrayal, privilege, and the devastating consequences of dangerous choices.

🎭 Genre: Crime • Drama • Thriller

⭐ IMDb: 5.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 33m • R

🎥 Director: Joel Schumacher

source_details.synopsis: Twelve is a 2010 teen crime drama film directed by Joel Schumacher from a screenplay by Jordan Melamed, based on Nick McDonell's 2002 novel of the same name. The film follows a young drug dealer whose luxurious lifestyle falls apart after his cousin is murdered and his best friend is arrested for the crime. It stars Chace Crawford, Rory Culkin, Curtis Jackson, Emily Meade, and Emma Roberts. Produced by Gaumont and Radar Pictures, the film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 29, 2010, and later released theatrically on August 6, 2010. A critical and commercial failure, it grossed $110,238 during its opening weekend and made $2.6 million worldwide, against a budget of $5 million
